title: Diagnosis and Fix for a Noisy Faucet: Cold Shut-off Valve, Washer Wear, and Pressure Considerations

summary: This Old House demonstrates a practical, step-by-step diagnostic approach to a noisy faucet caused by plumbing vibration. The video walks through isolating and testing the cold shut-off valve under the sink, explains why a partially closed valve can force water through a small opening and excite the valve washer, and then expands to other common culprits such as worn toilet fill valve washers, service valves versus ball valves, and overall home water pressure. The host also contrasts valve designs and offers targeted remedies, including keeping service valves fully open, recognizing the anatomy of a valve (stem and washer), and considering a pressure-reducing valve for high municipal pressure. The demonstrations emphasize listening for changes in noise as valves are manipulated and interpreted through simple mechanical reasoning.
topics: Fully open vs partially closed valve

sections.title: Isolate the cold shut-off valve and verify openness
sections.description: Demonstrates identifying the cold water shut-off under the sink, testing by opening the valve, and recognizing that a partially closed valve can cause vibration by forcing water through a restricted opening.

sections.title: Valve anatomy: stem and washer driving the flow
sections.description: Explains the stem and the washer at the bottom of a typical shut-off valve; shows how opening and closing the valve affects whether water can pass freely and why restriction can induce vibration.

sections.title: Other common culprits: toilet fill valve and pressure considerations
sections.description: Addresses the toilet fill valve washer as a frequent vibration source when worn, then discusses service valves under the sink, contrasts with a ball valve, and concludes with the role of a pressure-reducing valve to manage high incoming pressure.
